tables.how: From the tax returns on file for tax years 2020 to 2025: every contractor row filed by Lower Polk Community Benefit District, Japantown Community Benefit District and Ocean Avenue Association, and every contractor row in any return whose name reads NexStreet or Nextstreet. 6 rows name NexStreet, $2,552,654 in all: Japantown Community Benefit District Inc $172,337 (year to 2024-06-30); Japantown Community Benefit District Inc $235,968 (year to 2025-06-30); Lower Polk Community Benefit District $267,390 (year to 2022-06-30); Lower Polk Community Benefit District $237,797 (year to 2023-06-30); Lower Polk Community Benefit District $920,369 (year to 2025-06-30); Mid-Market Foundation $718,793 (year to 2024-12-31). Lower Polk's return for the year to June 2024 lists no contractor over $100,000. SOMA West Community Benefit District's returns are not in this extract.
tables.limits: A return is the organization's own statement, signed under penalty of perjury and not audited by the IRS. It lists only contractors paid more than $100,000 in the year (the five largest), so a smaller payment or a sixth contractor does not appear. The returns spell the firm three ways; they are treated as one firm because each names a cleaning and sanitation contractor called NexStreet. Nothing in a return shows whether the work was done or how the contractor was chosen: Lower Polk's own return says the vendor was selected through an open, public request for proposals, a record that has not been seen.

tables.how: Schedule L rows in the returns on file for Lower Polk Community Benefit District, Japantown Community Benefit District, Ocean Avenue Association and Mid Market Foundation, tax years 2020 to 2025. Lower Polk's rows name [the former Lower Polk director], whom it describes as its former executive director and now chief executive of the vendor; the others report no transaction with him or with NexStreet.
tables.limits: Schedule L is where an organization discloses business with its own insiders; Disclosure is what the form asks for. An organization that does not treat a person as its insider reports nothing, so the absence of a row at Japantown or Mid Market Foundation is not a statement that no tie exists. Rows about other people (a landlord on a board, a director's pay) are ordinary disclosures and are listed only so that everything these organizations reported can be seen.

sources.t: San Francisco Controller: Vendor Payments (Vouchers), fiscal 2019 to fiscal 2027 to date (DataSF)

tables.how: Every line of the Controller's payment file, fiscal 2019 to fiscal 2027 to date (to 9 November 2026), added up by payee, department, contract, purchasing rule and year. Two years are shown: the year the voucher was issued, read from its running number (scripts/lib/vouchers.py), and the fiscal year the file lists the line under, which for some lines is later. Kept: payees whose name begins Lower Polk Community Benefit, Japantown Community Benefit, SOMA West Community Benefit, Ocean Avenue Association or Mid Market Foundation. Payments from the department shown as General City are assessments the City collects from property owners and passes on. No payment line in the file is made out to NexStreet or to JIA Technologies (0 lines).
tables.limits: A payment is money paid for work under a contract, not a loss. The payment file starts in July 2018; near the turn of a year the voucher number dates a payment to within a few days. The City pays the districts; what a district then pays its own contractors is not in the City's file and is known only from the district's return.
